summary: Dharavandhoo Airport (DRV) is a small domestic airport located on the island of Dharavandhoo in Baa Atoll, Maldives. It serves as a key gateway for travelers heading to the resorts and guesthouses of Baa Atoll, including access to the renowned Hanifaru Bay UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. The airport features a single short runway and operates primarily through seaplane connections and short-haul domestic flights from Malé.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Dharavandhoo Airport?
A: Maldivian and Manta Air operate scheduled domestic flights connecting Dharavandhoo to Malé Velana International Airport and other regional destinations in the Maldives.

Q: How far is the airport from the nearest resorts?
A: Most resorts in Baa Atoll are accessible within 10 to 45 minutes by speedboat from Dharavandhoo, making it a convenient arrival point for the atoll.

Q: Can I take a seaplane from Dharavandhoo?
A: Seaplane transfers are typically arranged from Malé rather than Dharavandhoo, though speedboat transfers to nearby resorts are widely available from the airport.

Q: When is the best time to visit Baa Atoll?
A: The dry season from November to April offers calm seas and excellent visibility, while the southwest monsoon (May to October) is the best period for manta ray and whale shark encounters at Hanifaru Bay.
transport_tips: Speedboats are the primary mode of onward transport from Dharavandhoo and can be pre-arranged through your resort or guesthouse. Domestic flights to DRV are short, typically under 30 minutes from Malé, but schedules can be weather-dependent. Taxis on the island are limited; most accommodations arrange pickup directly from the airport terminal.
local_tip: Time your visit between June and October to experience the manta ray and whale shark feeding aggregations at nearby Hanifaru Bay, but book well in advance as visitor numbers are capped to protect the marine environment.
